facebook.long_form:
It's a big Saturday for COS families, and the headliner is free.

The Character Stroll at Acacia Park runs from 11 AM to 1 PM at no cost. You'll find Santa, the Grinch, Buddy the Elf, Elsa, and Anna — which means it'll be a hit for anyone from toddlers through early elementary. It's the kind of event worth showing up early for since it tends to draw a crowd.

Nearby, the Handmade HollyDays market is running from 9 AM with local vendors, food trucks, and live music. Good option for families who want to combine holiday shopping with something the kids can enjoy.

Over at the Garden of the Gods Visitor Center, History Day runs from 10 AM to 2 PM — a learning-focused experience in one of COS's best free outdoor settings. The Anastasia Musical Youth Edition is at the Ent Center for the Arts at 2 PM and again at 6:30 PM for families who want an afternoon or evening show.

stories.title: D11 Protesters Stage "Message Mile" March Over Superintendent Investigation

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text: COS parents marched a "Message Mile" Nov 10, demanding D11 release its investigation into Supt. Gaal and Deputy Supt. Comfort. District says litigation prevents it. Ongoing story with the $775M bond now live. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text: D11 says its investigation found no wrongdoing — but it can't release the report. Protesters aren't satisfied. A $775M bond is now live. If you're a D11 family, the accountability conversation is beginning. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Four days ago, parents and community members in Colorado Springs walked a "Message Mile" march to demand transparency from D11 leadership.

The focus: publicly releasing the findings of an independent third-party investigation into Superintendent Michael Gaal and Deputy Superintendent Terry Comfort. The district has consistently said the matter is in active litigation and can't be commented on — while also telling FOX21 that the investigation found no wrongdoing. That combination has not satisfied protesters.

This is unfolding against the backdrop of the $775 million bond measure D11 voters just approved — the largest bond in El Paso County history. An $80 million rebuild of Holmes Middle School is planned, and bond money will shape district facilities for a generation. For families in D11, the oversight structure matters.

The school board has proposed a citizen oversight committee to monitor how bond funds are spent. Whether that gets built and given real authority is worth watching over the next few months.

What do you think about how D11 is handling this situation?

stories.title: Taleco Gear Baby Jumpers and Swings Recalled — 41,100 Units, Fall and Strangulation Hazard

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text: RECALL: Taleco Gear baby jumpers & swings (#26-688) — ~41,100 units, sold on Amazon & Walmart. Fall & strangulation hazard. 52+ incidents, 32+ injuries. Full refund, destroy item. Check cpsc.gov/Recalls #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
If you have a Taleco Gear baby jumper or infant swing at home, stop using it today.

The Consumer Product Safety Commission recalled approximately 41,100 Taleco Gear baby jumpers and infant swings (recall #26-688, issued August 13, 2026). These were sold on Amazon, Walmart, and TalecoGear.com from April 2021 through July 2026. The products pose fall, impact, and strangulation hazards. CPSC received more than 52 incident reports and at least 32 injuries — including head bumps from falls.

The remedy is a full refund from Taleco Gear. The catch: the item needs to be destroyed, not donated, resold, or passed along to another family. This is an important detail — it means the product shouldn't end up at a consignment sale or thrift store.

If you're not sure whether you have a recalled item, go to cpsc.gov/Recalls and search "Taleco Gear" or recall number #26-688.

Do you check cpsc.gov/Recalls before buying or accepting baby gear as a gift? 🛡️

facebook.long_form:
If you're looking for something to do with a toddler tomorrow morning, the Cheyenne Mountain Zoo has you covered.

The Stroller Safari: Nocturnal November program runs Sunday, November 15, starting at 9 AM. It's one of the zoo's programs specifically designed for the stroller-and-young-toddler crowd — a guided, hands-on experience exploring nocturnal animals. For kids who can't yet handle a full-length zoo visit, this is exactly the right format: shorter, focused, and built for little attention spans.

It's also worth noting that the zoo's holiday programming season is about to begin, which means this is one of the last Sunday morning windows with a quieter, more relaxed vibe before the holiday lights crowds arrive.

stories.title: What to Actually Buy Kids for the Holidays — Age-Appropriate Toys and What Actually Works

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text: Holiday toy tip: age range labels mark CPSC small-part safety thresholds. For infants: no cords over 12 inches. For school-age kids: open-ended toys beat flashy ones. Check cpsc.gov/Recalls before buying. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Holiday shopping is in full swing — and with multiple product recalls active this season, it's a good time to revisit what actually makes a solid toy purchase for kids.

Start with the age range label. This isn't just a suggestion — it reflects CPSC testing thresholds for things like small parts and choking hazards. For infants and toddlers specifically, look for no strings or cords over 12 inches, materials that can be sanitized, and no small detachable pieces. If a product's age range doesn't match your child's age, the safety assumptions don't apply.

For school-age kids, the research consistently points in one direction: open-ended items hold attention longer. Building sets, art supplies, craft kits, and board games tend to outlast single-function electronic toys by a wide margin. Kids who can direct the play tend to stay more engaged.

The simplest gut check before any purchase: Can you describe what the child actually does with it? If the answer is "plays with it," that's a flag. If the answer is "builds towers and knocks them down" or "makes cards for the family," that's a toy.
